subject: Mutual Action Plan: cost assumptions & eval timeline — MediNova pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@medinova.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: MediNova pilot — MAP kickoff and cost sanity check

Hi Hannah / Ben,

Thanks again for yesterday’s demo — team was impressed with latency and the fallback story. We want to get a short mutual action plan (MAP) in place so procurement + engineering can align on evaluation criteria and an internal close target. Two asks from our side up front:

- Can you confirm an initial tokens-per-request and tokens-per-day estimate for our proposed transcript summarization flow (avg request ~450 tokens input, ~120 tokens output)?
- What caching/batching assumptions should we bake into our perf/cost model for the POC (we expect many repeated prefixes across users)?

We’d like to run a 3‑week eval beginning Feb 2, with procurement aiming to sign by Feb 27 if numbers align. Sharing some internal usage projections in a follow-up.

Best —
Jordan
Sr. Product Manager, MediNova
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@medinova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MediNova pilot — MAP kickoff and cost sanity check

Jordan —

Great to kick this off. High-level answers to help your financial model before we share the MAP draft:

- Tokens/request: based on your numbers (450 in / 120 out) we estimate ~570 tokens per request (including ~10 token overhead for delimiters).
- Baseline tokens/$ (hosted): currently using the model profile we demoed, the nominal cost is ~0.0009 USD per token (this is list — customers typically see lower in committed Dedicated pricing).
- Caching: for transcript summarization we typically see ~15–30% prefix reuse if customers dedupe/normalize text beforehand. With an LRU prefix cache (per-session) TTL of 10m we conservatively model 18% token savings for the POC.
- Batching: request batching for short sequences is less effective here; we recommend 1–2 request micro-batches for concurrent flows — model-level batching can reduce compute by ~8–12% depending on concurrency.

I’ll attach a draft MAP and a quick token-econ workbook. Ben, can you drop the internal per-token breakouts and an assumptions table?

Thanks,
Hannah
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Park <jordan.park@medinova.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MediNova pilot — MAP kickoff and cost sanity check

Jordan & team —

Putting numbers into the attached sheet (medinova-token-econ-model.xlsx). Key rows / assumptions I added:

- Avg tokens/request: 570 (as Hannah flagged).
- Requests/day (POC): two scenarios in the sheet — conservative 6k/day and optimistic 20k/day.
- Cache hit: 18% baseline, 30% optimistic if you run prefix normalization + client-side dedupe.
- Effective tokens/request after cache: 467 (18% savings).
- Batching savings: assume 10% compute reduction (model scheduling + micro-batching at 50–100ms windows). This is conservative — we can run an infra test to tighten this.
- Tokens per USD: sheet includes hosted list (0.0009) and a projected Dedicated rate (0.00055) for a 3‑month reserved pool.
- Non-token overheads: logging/retention and eval hooks add ~7% to total monthly cost in the model (we surfaced this separately).

I linked the live sheet in the MAP PDF and left editable comments. If you want, we can run a quick benchmark on a representative shard of transcripts to validate the 18% cache hit and the 10% batching benefit.

—Ben
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachment: medinova-token-econ-model.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@medinova.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MediNova pilot — MAP kickoff and cost sanity check

Thanks Ben — useful breakdown. Couple of clarifying points from engineering/procurement:

1) Volume shape: bulk of our 20k estimate is long-tail (sporadic clinicians) — steady-state concurrency per shard likely <150 qps.
2) Quality gating: procurement wants to tie pricing to a validation set — can we freeze an eval prompt set and have automatic regression alerts?
3) Fallbacks: what's the recommended fallback policy when Dedicated capacity is saturated? (preferred behavior is degrade to a cheaper, smaller model rather than dropping requests).

If we can map these into the MAP and get a brief SLA note, procurement will feel comfortable targeting Feb 27 sign.

—Jordan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@medinova.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 09:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MediNova pilot — MAP kickoff and cost sanity check

Jordan — quick runtime note from infra:

- Concurrency profile you described (<150 qps) is manageable in Dedicated. We recommend enabling model-variant fallback (primary -> cost-optimized clipped variant) with soft timeouts (2000ms) to avoid request drops. That fallback should reduce token cost per request by ~12% (smaller context / shorter output truncation) but can impact summarization brevity — include in acceptance criteria.
- Quantization: if you plan to use Dedicated GPUs with int8 quant, expect a small delta in generation tokens (noise) — we capture this as ±2% in the model.
- Cache config: default prefix cache TTL 10m, per-session namespace. For your long-tail traffic, consider a small shared prefix cache for common templates (50k entries) — expect incremental 5–8% savings.

I’ll add a bullet about automatic eval/regression alerts — we can ship a webhook to your evaluation runner that triggers on metric drift.

—Karthik
Lead, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@medinova.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@medinova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 14:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MediNova pilot — MAP kickoff and cost sanity check

Jordan / Marta —

Thanks — attaching the MAP draft (mnp_map_draft.pdf) and the token-econ workbook we referenced. Quick agreed next steps so procurement/engineering can work the timelines:

1) Week of Jan 26 — Redwood to run targeted perf benchmark (sample shard from MediNova) and validate cache hit assumption (owner: Ben).
2) Feb 2–20 — 3-week evaluation window using the frozen prompt set (owner: MediNova + Redwood integration lead). We will provision a Dedicated pilot pool and enable model-variant fallback.
3) Feb 23–27 — Procurement reviews final econ; target contract signature by Feb 27.

Acceptance criteria to include in the MAP:
- Regression tolerance: <1.5% degradation on ROUGE-L / summary length relative to baseline on the frozen eval set.
- Cost gating: projected tokens/$ delta > 15% vs hosted list should trigger a joint review and an optional 1-week extension to the eval.

We’ll upload the validated benchmark results and a short benchmark report to the Drive link in the MAP. If that schedule looks good I’ll ask Legal to prepare an initial SOW + draft pricing decks for the Feb 23 review.

Best,
Hannah
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachments: mnp_map_draft.pdf, medinova-token-econ-model.xlsx
